warnings: Preformed vitamin A from supplements, liver and fortified foods should stay below 3000 µg per day for adults.
Beta-carotene from fruits and vegetables does not count toward the upper limit.
Pregnancy: avoid vitamin A supplements, fish liver oil and liver unless a doctor advises them; high preformed vitamin A can cause birth defects.
Age 60+ and people at risk of osteoporosis: UK NHS advises keeping total vitamin A at or below about 1500 µg per day.
Smokers and ex-smokers should avoid high-dose beta-carotene supplements (raised lung cancer risk in trials).
Do not combine vitamin A supplements with oral retinoid medicines; check with a doctor if taking blood thinners, fat-blocking weight-loss drugs or liver-affecting medicines.
A 50 g portion of goat liver can exceed the daily upper limit; limit liver to about once a week and avoid vitamin A supplements in that week.
General information, not medical advice. Check with a doctor before starting supplements.
Preformed vitamin A (retinol and esters) from supplements, liver and fortified foods must stay at or below 3,000 µg per day from all sources.
Carotenoids from fruits and vegetables do not count toward the upper limit; skin tinting from carrots or papaya is harmless.
Pregnancy or planning pregnancy: avoid vitamin A supplements, fish-liver oil and liver unless a doctor prescribes them; high preformed vitamin A can cause birth defects.
Age 50+, post-menopause or osteoporosis: NHS advises staying at or below about 1,500 µg per day from food and supplements and liver no more than once a week.
Smokers and ex-smokers should avoid high-dose beta-carotene and retinyl palmitate supplements (more lung cancer in trials).

Do not combine vitamin A supplements with oral retinoids (isotretinoin, acitretin); check with a doctor if taking blood thinners, orlistat or liver-affecting medicines, or with kidney or liver disease.
A 50 g portion of goat liver is about 7,800 µg and exceeds the daily upper limit; chicken liver 50 g is about 1,700 µg.

ICMR-NIN 2020 values are from search snippets and summaries (secondary, unverified); the pregnancy RDA of 900 µg looks low against the stated extra allowance and should be checked in the printed report.
Plant carotenoids are counted at ICMR 6:1; isotope studies suggest less conversion (spinach about 21:1, carrot about 15:1), so plant-only totals are 'on paper'.
IFCT has no retinol for milk, curd, paneer or ghee and has suspect values for dry dates, pink-skin sweet potato and Tholam fish; do not use them unchecked.
